title: Passage: A Roman day
standardSummary: Read a longer mixed-grammar passage; answer detailed comprehension questions.
teach: Longer connected Latin for reading power.

passage.title: A short Roman day
passage.latin:
Māne servus aquam ad vīllam portat.
Dominus, quī in urbe habitat, ad forum venit.
Multī cīvēs lēgēs audiunt.
Posteā mīlitēs, quī arma ceperant, ad castra redeunt.
Nocte pāx in viīs est — sed nōn semper.
passage.notes: māne = morning · posteā = afterward · nocte = at night · viīs = streets/roads · Use known vocabulary; guess from context only if needed.

sampleAnswers: In the morning a servant brings water. The master goes to the forum; citizens hear laws. Soldiers who had taken arms return to camp; at night there is peace—but not always.
Daily life then soldiers and fragile peace.
